title: 3.1 Permutations and combinations

q.Q1: Q1. A café offers 3 drinks, 4 main dishes and 2 desserts. How many different meals of one of each are possible?
q.Q2: Q2. How many 3-letter codes can be formed from A–E if letters cannot be repeated?

q.Q3: Q3. In how many ways can 5 learners line up for a photo?
q.Q4: Q4. A race has 10 runners. In how many ways can gold, silver and bronze be awarded?

q.Q5: Q5. A committee of 3 is chosen from 7 people. How many committees are possible?

q.Q7: Q7. A team of 4 is chosen from 6 boys and 5 girls. How many teams have exactly 2 girls?
q.Q8: Q8. How many different arrangements of the letters of KENYA are possible?

q.Q9: Q9. A coach picks 11 players from a squad of 16. How many line-ups are possible if the captain must play?

q.Exit ticket: Exit ticket. State the difference between a permutation and a combination.
